answer: An agent economy can charge every identity a refundable stake before it can trade. A juniper seller and a dune hauler each lock the same deposit, and the network slashes it when an agent cheats or spams orders. A fake army then stops being free: each copy needs its own stake, and a mirror trick that clones one reputation across many accounts fails because the stake cannot be spent twice. Attackers pay per identity, so honest agents stay cheaper to run than a swarm of fakes.
